subject.title: Synchronous transcript I/O scales with tool-result payload size and can block the event loop the liveness monitor samples

question: Should maintainers require current-main liveness measurement before approving an async active-transcript persistence refactor, or sponsor the refactor based on the source-backed blocking path alone?
rationale: The synchronous path is clearly reachable, but the exact false-abort causal chain depends on payload caps, event-loop timing, and stuck-session recovery state that were not live-proven on current main.

options.title: Require Measurement First
options.body: Keep this open for a controlled large-tool-result run that records eventLoopDelayMaxMs and any recovery classifications before changing the persistence contract.

options.title: Sponsor Async Persistence Now
options.body: Approve an owner-guided refactor of active SessionManager writes with broad session, compaction, repair, and diagnostic regression coverage.

options.title: Fold Into Liveness Work
options.body: Track the transcript-write source as part of the broader liveness recovery issue while keeping this issue linked for the specific persistence cause.

recommendation.title: Require Measurement First
recommendation.body: Keep this open for a controlled large-tool-result run that records eventLoopDelayMaxMs and any recovery classifications before changing the persistence contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant recent ownership signal is the transcript writer seam and lock-ordering work needed for a safe persistence refactor.
